comments.author: @RADCreativeArt
comments.text: Interesting documentary on NJ, but having lived here for 63 years, just 30 mins from AC, it’s not as glamorous or exciting as this makes it look. The only shore I feel safe is Cape May. I don’t have to walk the shops with a can of pepper spray in my pocket…

replies.author: @mariabernard8726
replies.text:
It is interesting because I moved to AC over two decades ago and could always see the potential of the city; it is taking some Jersey time but is getting there. Regarding safety, I have never felt unsafe here. There are some spots you do not go, like in any other city; yes, even in Zurich, Switzerland, there are streets where you know not to walk by yourself in the middle of the night. 
In short: People tend to always think the grass is greener on the other side of the fence.

replies.author: @sailingspark9748
replies.text: If you do not feel safe walking in Stone Harbor, Avalon, Ocean City, or Brigantine, there is something wrong. The really only unsafe shore town is Atlantic City and even that is not too bad if you know the areas to stay away from. (hint, they are far from the tourist areas)

replies.author: @my1ernest
replies.text: I have lived in NJ for 26 years. I was born in NYC and moved here when I was 37 years old. Ever since I was a little girl I wanted to move from there. I hated being surrounded by tall skyscrapers and people crunched together walking down the streets. For many of the things that make people from all over the world dream to visit New York City, when you're born and lived there a good portion of your life it's just ho-hum seeing those famous sites that NYC is famous for. I fell in love with NJ as soon as I moved here. Whenever I need to go visit the city all I have to do is jump on a train or bus and I'm there within an hour.
